note: First Surface knowledge table. Rows are rules for the road surface; later tickets add rows (kerb, sidewalk, ground). Every number names its source or is marked (estimate).

class_wear.source: (estimate) rank of traffic volume by OSM highway class; wear scales the wheel-path and oil-strip strength

wheel_path.source: (estimate) US passenger-car track width is 1.5 to 1.65 m, so each wheel path centres about 0.75 to 0.8 m from the lane centre; FHWA pavement-distress surveys place the wheel paths in the same two bands

oil_strip.source: (estimate) drip band between the wheel paths of a lane, about the width of an engine bay's oil pan

age.source: Pomerantz et al., Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, 'Paving Materials for Heat Island Mitigation' (2000): new asphalt solar reflectance about 0.05, oxidised and worn about 0.10 to 0.15; the multipliers scale the 0.085 base tint to that span
age.per_tile: age = range[0] + (range[1] - range[0]) * hash(TileSeed): roads are resurfaced on a 10 to 20 year cycle (estimate), so neighbouring tiles differ

dry_climate.source: (estimate) strong sun and little rain oxidise binder faster, so dry-climate roads (GrassDry near 1) read lighter and greyer

pool.source: Poly Haven, CC0 (credited in CREDITS.md); a stretch picks one member, an orientation and a scale from its hash
